newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Former Bond Corp director Mitchell sent to jail.
newsitem.headline: Former Bond Corp director Mitchell sent to jail.

text.p: Former Bond Corp Holdings Ltd director Peter Mitchell was sentenced to four years jail on Friday for his part in the A$1.4 billion Bell Resources Ltd fraud.
The charges were brought by the Australian Securities Commission (ASC), which described the sentence as appropriate.

Mitchell had pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Western Australia to four charges of misusing his position as a director to help strip A$1.4 billion in cash from Bell Resources following its takeover by Bond Corp in 1988.
He will be eligible for parole in 16 months.
Bond Corp chairman and entrepreneur Alan Bond was also sentenced in February to four years jail on cash-stripping offences, with parole possible next year.
The ASC said charges were pending against another former Bond Corp director, Tony Oates, who was detained by Polish authorites and was awaiting a decision on his extradition.
ASC chairman Alan Cameron said the conviction "sent a message to corporate Australia that custodial sentences will be handed down by the judiciary for serious corporate crimes."
